einzeiler: A curated preview of standout book releases hitting shelves this September.
kurzfassung: The team from The Bookshelf in Thomasville presents a curated selection of notable book releases scheduled for September. The hosts discuss an array of character-driven fiction, memoirs, and thrillers, offering personal insights on each title. Listeners can purchase the featured books using a special discount code provided in the episode show notes.
stichpunkte: Preview of major book releases arriving in September 2023
Discussion of Meg Howry's character-driven novel Body Language
Exploration of Chloe Benjamin's Antarctica-set novel The Understory
Overview of Emma Klein's novel Switzy, longlisted for the Booker Prize
Review of Kate Stammen London's political rom-com See You Next Tuesday
Introduction to Megan E. Freeman's young adult novel in verse The Secret to Belonging
Highlighting Katie Clapham's independent bookstore memoir Receipts from the Bookshop
Examination of Kelly McWilliams' historical fiction novel American Nightmare
Discussion of Abby Jenny's thriller Children of the Wolf
Preview of Robert Kolker's nonfiction family study The Vanishing Family

clips.hook: A super El Nino is affecting weather globally.
clips.text: The speakers discuss an unusually large El Nino event that is expected to have widespread global impacts.

clips.hook: Breaking two reading rules for one exceptionally long book.
clips.text: The host admits to breaking personal reading rules by tackling a massive novel that exceeds five hundred pages without chapter breaks.

clips.hook: Traveling to Switzerland for a final time.
clips.text: The plot centers on a protagonist taking a borrowed plane to Switzerland under mysterious and significant circumstances.

clips.hook: Finding sudden acceptance in a study abroad program in Norway.
clips.text: A protagonist who feels neglected at home travels to Norway for a scholarship program, where she quickly adapts and receives immense warmth from a host family.

clips.hook: A thriller focused on choices rather than whodunits.
clips.text: The appeal of a specific thriller lies in the protagonist's decisions after the culprit's identity is revealed early in the story.

beschreibung:
This week on From the Front Porch, it’s a New Release Rundown! Annie, Erin, and Olivia share the September releases they’re excited about to help you build your TBR. When you purchase or preorder any of the books they talk about, enter the code NEWRELEASEPLEASE at checkout for 10% off your order!

To purchase the books mentioned in this episode, stop by The Bookshelf in Thomasville, visit our website (search episode 597), or download and shop on The Bookshelf’s official app:

Annie’s books

Body Language by Meg Howrey

Tom Lake by Ann Patchett and Like Mother, Like Mother by Susan Rieger

The Wanderers and They're Going To Love You by Meg Howrey

See You Next Tuesday by Kate Stayman-London (Releases September 8th, 2026)

One to Watch by Kate Stayman-London

Big Fan by Michael Schur and Joe Posnanski, The Hopefuls, Everything’s Fine by Cecilia Rabess

American Nightmare by Kelly McWilliams (Releases September 15th, 2026)

Ring Shout by P. Djeli Clark

Olivia’s books

Under Story by Chloe Benjamin

The Secret to Belonging by Megan E Freeman (Releases September 15th, 2026)

Children of the Wolf by Abby Geni (Releases September 15th, 2026)

Erin’s books

Switzy by Emma Cline (Releases September 8th, 2026)

Receipts from the Bookshop by Katie Clapham (Releases September 8th, 2026)

The Vanishing Family by Robert Kolker (Releases September 29th, 2026)

From the Front Porch is a weekly podcast production of The Bookshelf, an independent bookstore in South Georgia. You can follow The Bookshelf’s daily happenings on Instagram and Facebook, and all the books from today’s episode can be purchased online through our store website, www.bookshelfthomasville.com.

A full transcript of today’s episode can be found here.
